title: PG-W-21A Trust records, an eligibility gate and audit events for federated trust governance (memev)
request: Programme contract PG-W-21A in memev: trust records, an eligibility gate and audit events for trust governance in the federated model. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. The id is in the style of SO-W-08B: its second part starts with a letter, so the redteam gate's specIdOf reads the whole name and the contract has its own record path; the work package number 21 is not in docs/scope-one/programme/fragments. Why: work breakdown rows 4.3.7 and 4.3.8 are blocked in part because trust governance, the second of the two integrations the addendum names beside the merge boundary, has no definition in this repository. The definition is proposed in ADR 8 (docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md, with the full text in docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md), status proposed and every product choice in it provisional. This contract builds only the part that does not depend on the owner's answers: the trust record data model and schema, the evaluation, the audit events, the interfaces between admission, findings and actor resolution, and the boundary tests. Boundaries: (1) the admission service and the admission adapter are SO-F-03.3 and SO-F-08 and are not repeated; this contract adds one check for the external hook and a rule for composing checks there. (2) The relationship and policy evaluation is SO-F-04; a relationship is the edge between two nodes, a trust record says which subjects behind an edge are eligible for what. (3) Admission of nodes and agents to a site (WP09-01 of PG-09.1) and exclusion on equivocation (WP09-03) are not repeated; this contract refuses nothing they accept and excludes nothing. (4) The trust adapter boundary is WP09-02 of PG-09.1 and the trust service specification is the signed vault contract WO-05-D, cited by id; this contract does not specify the service and names no product. (5) The finding model is SO-F-09.2 and the actor resolution is resolveActor of SO-F-09.2; this contract reads the actor and changes no finding code. (6) Cross-organisation trust is WP13-05 of PG-13.1 and stays deferred. (7) crdt-merge stays in its own repository behind the call-out boundary (ADR 6, decided); nothing here touches it. (8) Finding operations replayed from the log still trust the by field until the first finding writer goes through Graph.bindFindingEvent (pull request #362); that is an open follow-up in docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md that blocks that writer, it is not closed here, and the trust book reads only resolved actors on its write path. Deferred: every requirement marked DEFERRED waits for an owner answer named in the ADR: the trust root (question 1), cross-organisation trust (2), the default for a new device (3), revocation across nodes (4), any tier gate (5), the final rule for who may grant (6), further purposes (7), the effect on admitted history (8), delegation in the first release (9) and the external trust service (10). The topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6 stays OPEN and is an input to none of this. No production caller: the modules are libraries with tests. The Admission they plug into has no production caller on main until it is wired, so the wiring of the book and the composed gate into the vault is one follow-up after questions 1 and 4 are answered, recorded as deferred in WP21-03; this is the position SR-1.15 asks to be stated, not a waiver of it. Order: WP21-01 starts now; WP21-02 starts once pull request #362 merges (isResolvedActor); WP21-03 starts once pull requests #358 and #362 merge (the Admission and the actor). Depends on contracts: SO-F-01 (the subject and scope model), SO-F-03.3, SO-F-04, SO-F-08, SO-F-09.2. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier. Nothing in this contract decides ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 or SO-A-05, and it adds no role-by-action matrix.

tasks.title: Trust record, version 1: the grant and revocation records, their validator and schema, and a pure evaluation that denies by default, lets delegation only narrow, and cascades revocation, as of a stated time
requirements: a trust record has schema 'memev-trust/1' and one of two kinds. A grant names its id, the subject trusted, the issuer, one scope, the purposes it covers (a closed list of two in version 1: contribute and verify), a start, a required expiry after the start, optional evidence references (at most 8, each a text of at most 128 characters) and an optional delegation block { depth (a whole number, 0 or more), parent (a grant id, optional) }. A revocation names its id, the grant it revokes, its issuer, a time and a reason from a closed list (compromised, left, error, other). PROVISIONAL until the owner decides ADR 8 (source: docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md, section How trust is granted, scoped, delegated, revoked and audited)

the validator refuses a record with an unknown field, a subject or issuer that is not a subject id of one of the six types of src/engine/identity.mjs, a personal scope (a personal scope is never shared), a scope that validateScope refuses, an empty or unknown purpose, an expiry that is missing or not after the start, evidence over the limits, and a delegation depth that is not a whole number of 0 or more (source: src/engine/identity.mjs:13-14, :66-75; docs/FEDERATION.md:147-151)

evaluate(request { subject, scope, purpose }, { records, roots, at }) returns { eligible, rule, reason, chain } and denies by default: no records, no roots, a grant whose issuer is neither a root nor the holder of a live delegating grant, a purpose or a scope the grant does not name, a time before the start or at or after the expiry, a revoked grant and an invalid request each deny with a rule id. A root is a subject id the caller passes in; there is no default root and no default grant for any subject, device or node. At is required: there is no default to the clock (source: docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md:66-67, deny by default as the safe default of ADR 5, which is not decided; docs/FEDERATION.md:228-230; addendum line 335)

a delegated grant only narrows its parent: the same scope, the same or fewer purposes, an expiry no later than the parent's, and a depth lower than the parent's; a parent of depth 0 cannot delegate. A revocation takes effect from its time, so an evaluation at an earlier time is unchanged, and revoking a grant makes every grant delegated from it ineligible (source: addendum line 274; docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md)

the module is pure: it reads and writes no file, no network and no clock, imports only src/engine/identity.mjs, and does not change its inputs (source: addendum lines 333 to 335, trust is not a store and not access)
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 1, the trust root model): which subject a node accepts as a root; this task takes the roots as a parameter and decides none
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 3, the default for a new device): any automatic or low-level grant for a new device; this task grants nothing by default
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 7, purposes and verification requirements): any purpose beyond contribute and verify, and any required-verification level
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 9, delegation in the first release): whether the delegation block is accepted by a shipped command; this task defines and tests the record only
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Starts at once: it depends on nothing that is not on main (src/engine/identity.mjs). Defines the trust record and the one function that answers whether a subject is eligible for a purpose in a scope as of a time. It writes nothing, reads no store and has no caller outside its tests: it has no production caller in this task, the same position as the admission it will plug into until that is wired, and the production wiring is deferred (see the request). Trust is an eligibility input only: nothing here grants a permission, a membership or a read. The schema file docs/schemas/trust-record-v1.json lists the same fields as the validator.

tasks.title: The trust book over the operation log: grants and revocations written only with a resolved actor, authority held in one provisional table, events as the only store, and a frozen read-only reader
requirements: a TrustBook is made over the vault's operation log (append and iterate, the shape the Admission of SO-F-03.3 takes), with the roots as a parameter; it appends one trust.granted or trust.revoked event for each accepted record and rebuilds its state from those events when it is made, so a restart gives the same decisions and there is no store but the log (source: the Admission of SO-F-03.3, pull request #358 at 7bc87da, admission.mjs lines 11 to 13 and 44; docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md:93-95, ADR 7, proposed)

a grant or a revocation is written only with a resolved actor: the object isResolvedActor of src/engine/identity.mjs recognises, as SO-F-09.2 resolves it (pull request #362 at c85d4c5). An object of the same shape that resolveActor did not make is refused. The issuer is the actor's subject id, never a field of the payload: a record naming another issuer is refused (source: SO-F-09.2 criterion on a forged by)

who may write trust is one frozen table, GRANT_AUTHORITY, of subject types, and it is PROVISIONAL: a person or an operator subject, and no agent, service, device or node, until the permission matrix (ADR 5, open) and the decision workflow (SO-A-05) are decided; deciding them changes this table and nothing else (source: SO-F-09.2, the same provisional rule for dismissal; docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md:59-67)
an event holds the validated record and nothing else: evidence is references only, within the limits of WP21-01; the book never copies content of a contribution into an event

reader() returns a frozen object with one member, eligible(request), that answers from the book's current state at a time the caller gives and returns a copy; the reader has no grant, revoke or log member and cannot reach the log or the book (source: the read-only reader of PG-19.2, Vault#tasksReader; addendum line 341)
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 6, who may grant and revoke): the final rule; this task ships the provisional table only

DEFERRED (ADR 8 questions 1, 2 and 4, the trust root, trust across organisations and revocation across nodes): a record from another node is not read, applied or sent; this task has no import or export of records

tasks.title: Admission, findings and actors meet the trust book: an eligibility gate for the Admission external hook, one composition rule for checks on that hook, revalidation requests after a revocation, and boundary tests
requirements: eligibilityGate({ reader, now }) returns a function of an envelope that the Admission external option accepts: { ok: true } or { ok: false, code, reason }, where code is the trust rule id. It asks reader.eligible for the purpose contribute, for the subject and the scope of the contribution. A refusal is a federation.rejected event with step external and no payload; a pass skips no later step, so signature, authority and replay still run (source: SO-F-08, trust read only as an eligibility input; Admission of SO-F-03.3, admission.mjs lines 4 to 9 and 95 to 108)

composeExternal(...checks) returns one function of the same shape: the checks run in the order given, the first refusal is the answer and later checks are not called, a check that throws is a refusal with a code of its own, and an empty list passes everything and leaves the Admission events as they are without it (source: the open follow-up 'Two users of the Admission external hook' in docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md; SO-F-04 relationshipGate, pull request #368 at 8d3bbbc, policy.mjs lines 107 to 115)
work queued before a revocation and offered after it is refused, because the gate asks at the time of admission (source: docs/FEDERATION.md:251)

after a revocation, revalidationRequests({ subject, scope, since }) appends one trust.revalidation_requested event for each contribution the node admitted for that subject in that scope since the time, naming its operation id, sender, sequence, subject and scope; a second run appends none; it changes, reverses and quarantines nothing and does nothing for any other subject (source: addendum line 381, affected contributions identified for review and revalidation; docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md)

the boundaries: trust never grants (a subject with a live contribute grant and no membership is refused at the authority step, and a revoked or expired subject is refused whatever the book says); a personal scope is never shared; the trust modules import nothing from src/engine/merge.mjs and no crdt-merge package, send nothing across the call-out boundary, and leave src/engine/merge.mjs and src/cli/sync.mjs unchanged; with no gate configured, or an empty composition, Admission behaves as before; with a reader that throws, the gate refuses and the event says why (source: ADR 6, decided; docs/PAID-TRUST.md:38-40; docs/FEDERATION.md:147-151, :258-259; addendum lines 343 and 382)
the finding path reads trust through the same reader.eligible with the purpose verify; this task changes no finding code
DEFERRED (ADR 8 question 8, the effect of a revocation on admitted history): anything beyond a revalidation request, such as marking, hiding or quarantining a contribution
DEFERRED (ADR 8 questions 5 and 10, the tier and the external trust service): any tier or licence gate, and any call to the external trust service
DEFERRED (SO-F-09.2 and ADR 5, who may verify and dismiss): the call from the finding code to the reader; it waits for the permission matrix and the decision workflow, both open

DEFERRED (production wiring): constructing the book in the vault and giving the composed gate to the production Admission; this contract has no production caller by design, as the Admission it plugs into has none on main until it is wired, and the wiring is one follow-up after the owner answers questions 1 and 4
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Starts once pull requests #358 (SO-F-03.3, the Admission) and #362 (SO-F-09.2, the actor) merge, and builds on WP21-02. Its tests build an Admission over a real operation log and a real identity document, as the admission tests of SO-F-03.3 do, and carry each envelope to it themselves; no network route is added. The gate and the composition are plain functions of an envelope; the revalidation request is an event, not an action on the contribution.
